name: web-app
raw_brief_text: For a human-computer interaction course, build a small responsive web application for recording and reviewing university laboratory experiments. A student can create an experiment with a title, date, research question, and notes, then list experiments newest-first and filter the list by a case-insensitive title substring. Provide server-side validation, accessible labels, an empty state, and a local setup guide. Use a Python HTTP API and a browser UI; all data may be stored locally and the app must work without external services.
rubric_text: 1. Automated: Creating, listing, sorting, and case-insensitive filtering return the expected records. 2. Automated: Missing title and invalid date are rejected with field-specific errors. 3. Human judgment: Keyboard and screen-reader interaction is understandable.

project_spec.title: Laboratory Experiment Log Web App
project_spec.description: Build a local-first responsive web application for recording and reviewing university laboratory experiments through a Python HTTP API and browser UI. Support creation, newest-first listing, case-insensitive title filtering, validation, accessible labels, an empty state, and local setup documentation.
deliverables: A Python HTTP API for creating and listing laboratory experiment records.
A browser UI for creating records and filtering a newest-first experiment list.
Field-specific validation for required titles and valid dates.
Automated behavior tests and a local setup guide.
constraints: Store data locally and require no external services.
Experiment records include title, date, research question, and notes.
The UI provides accessible labels and an explicit empty state.

rubric_items.criterion: Creating, listing, sorting, and case-insensitive filtering return the expected records.
rubric_items.check_method: API and UI tests create fixed records and assert newest-first order and case-insensitive title-filter results.

rubric_items.criterion: Missing title and invalid date are rejected with field-specific errors.
rubric_items.check_method: Submit a missing title and an invalid date independently and assert the response identifies the corresponding field.

rubric_items.criterion: Keyboard and screen-reader interaction is understandable.
rubric_items.check_method: A reviewer navigates the creation form, filters, and empty state with a keyboard and screen reader.

planner_response.plan_summary: Build the local persistence and Python API first, then the accessible browser interface, automated checks, and setup documentation.
evidence: All requested record fields, create/list/filter/sort behavior, validation, accessibility, empty state, local-only storage, tests, and setup guide are assigned to tasks.

nodes.description: Define the experiment record and initialize local persistence without external services.
acceptance_criteria: A persisted record round-trips title, ISO date, research question, and notes without losing Unicode text.

nodes.description: Implement the create endpoint and field-specific server-side validation.
acceptance_criteria: A valid create request returns the stored experiment and a missing title returns a field-specific 4xx error.
An invalid date request returns a field-specific 4xx error without creating a record.

nodes.description: Implement newest-first listing and case-insensitive title-substring filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Listing two records returns descending ISO dates and filtering matches a title regardless of query case.

nodes.description: Build the experiment creation form with accessible labels and validation feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Every input has a programmatically associated label and validation errors are announced beside the field.

nodes.description: Build the newest-first list, title filter, and explicit empty state.
acceptance_criteria: The UI shows newest-first records, filters titles without case sensitivity, and displays an empty-state message for zero results.

nodes.description: Style the record form and list for narrow and desktop browser viewports.
acceptance_criteria: At viewport widths of 375 and 1280 pixels, the form and list remain visible without horizontal page overflow.

nodes.description: Add API and browser behavior tests for creation, filtering, order, and validation.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests assert create/list/filter results, newest-first ordering, and both field-specific validation failures.

nodes.description: Document local installation, startup, and the experiment workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout can follow the README commands to start the API and UI without configuring a remote service.
